solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spring team, number lost

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so the abbreviation that follows drops out of the word

blocks.note: a span is a pair of horses or oxen yoked together
N is the standard abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A sports side heading into spring has lost one of its players.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N from SPAN to leave SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral water source, a natural spring often visited for health treatments.

clue.text: Double provided, indifferent

blocks.note: so can mean provided (that); doubled it is written twice

explanation.surface: A cautious bet on a double, placed only on condition, by someone who barely cares.
explanation.definitionFit: Something middling or mediocre is described as so-so, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Coin, not English – it was worth little abroad

definitions.text: Coin, not English – it was worth little abroad

indicators.note: not tells us to go without the abbreviation that follows, so it is removed

blocks.note: a piece is a coin, as in a fifty-pence piece
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A coin that is not English was worth very little in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: PIECE loses its E. The whole clue doubles as the definition: the pice was a tiny Indian coin, so it is both a non-English coin and one worth little abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The pice was a small copper coin of British India, a quarter of an anna, of very low value.

clue.text: Lack of coordination always interrupted by exercise?

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: ay (or aye) is an old and poetic word for always
to tax is to exercise or put a strain on, as in taxing the brain

explanation.surface: Someone forever clumsy, with physical training perhaps the culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that exercise is used in the less obvious sense of strain or tax, as in exercising the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxy (ataxia) is the medical term for loss of muscular control and coordinated movement.

clue.text: Messy sops and so on at an end in covered bowl (9, two words)

indicators.note: a messy thing is jumbled up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
etc is the abbreviation of et cetera, and so on
time is up when it is at an end

explanation.surface: Soggy bread sops and the like left over at the end of a meal in a lidded dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A posset is a hot drink of milk curdled with wine or ale, once taken from a special cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A posset cup was a lidded two-handled vessel for serving posset, so a covered bowl describes it.

clue.text: Aussie narcotic? It's served in a small cake

indicators.note: something served in a dish sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a puri is a small round Indian bread, deep-fried and puffed

explanation.surface: A drug smuggled to the diner baked inside a little cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The cake is Indian fried bread, not a sweet bake.
explanation.definitionFit: Pituri is an Australian shrub whose nicotine-rich leaves Aboriginal people chewed as a stimulant drug.

clue.text: Advocate of power to the people brandishing torch with coal

definitions.text: Advocate of power to the people

indicators.note: brandishing means waving wildly about, so the following letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolutionary agitator waving a flaming torch and burning coal before the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's mob with torches fits the answer neatly: ochlocracy is rule by the mob.
explanation.definitionFit: An ochlocrat favours ochlocracy, government by the mob or the masses, power handed to the populace.

clue.text: Institution, right to replace old black stone

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so one letter is swapped in where another stood

blocks.note: a school is an educational institution
R is the abbreviation for right
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An establishment rightly replacing an old black monument stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second O of SCHOOL becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Schorl is black tourmaline, a dark mineral found in granites.

clue.text: Gardener giving off unpleasant smell? He was due to follow the chief

definitions.text: He was due to follow the chief

indicators.note: giving off means sending out, so the abbreviation that follows leaves the word

blocks.note: a botanist studies plants, playfully called a gardener
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A smelly gardener, followed by an heir waiting on a clan leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove BO from BOTANIST. The question mark warns that a botanist is only loosely a gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Celtic custom a tanist was the elected heir who succeeded a chieftain on his death.

clue.text: Fuss formerly created by one in grip of depression

indicators.note: a thing in the grip of another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a col is a dip or pass between two mountain peaks

explanation.surface: A past commotion stirred up by somebody suffering from depression.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside COL; the depression is in the landscape, not the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Coil once meant tumult or a noisy disturbance, as in Hamlet's 'mortal coil'.

clue.text: Piano board

blocks.note: the bare definition of the competition word
in a plain competition puzzle solvers write this clue themselves, so only a definition is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was the competition word: Azed prints only a definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalier is a keyboard worked by the feet, fitted beneath a piano to add organ-style bass notes.

clue.text: Oil-yielding tree here in Marseille occupied by wild coati

indicators.note: a place occupied by someone has them inside it, so one piece sits within the other
wild suggests out of control, so the animal's letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
ici is French for here, and Marseille is in France

explanation.surface: A tree in a southern French city where a wild raccoon-like animal has made its home.
explanation.walkthrough: A coati is a South American relative of the raccoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiticica is a Brazilian tree whose seeds give a drying oil used in paints and varnishes.

clue.text: Coat for youngster peels off and is taken inside

indicators.note: off here means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of the verb are rearranged
taken inside means brought within, so the short word goes into the middle of the jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child strips off a coat and is brought indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long cloak or coat, in one sense a child's outdoor garment over other clothes.

clue.text: Female bandaging pet's injury once

indicators.note: bandaging wraps something round, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: she is a female person
a cat is a common pet; the 's is read as is, linking to what follows

explanation.surface: A woman dressing her animal's wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathe is an old noun for harm or damage, surviving today in unscathed.

clue.text: Like seductive language that is cloaked in old-fashioned script

indicators.note: something cloaked in a garment is wrapped up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
hond is an obsolete spelling of hand, as in handwriting

explanation.surface: Sweet talk dressed up in quaint antique lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand means handwriting here, and hond is its obsolete spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Honied (honeyed) words are sweet and flattering, the coaxing speech of someone trying to win you over.

clue.text: Coarsest part of flax, unfavourable in the end

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: ill can mean unfavourable, as in an ill wind
a coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music

explanation.surface: The poorest fibre of the flax plant, a bad sign at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The end is a musical one: the closing passage of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Codilla is the coarse tow or waste fibre left from hemp or flax after dressing.

clue.text: A rum diet – tons imbibed, all mixed in old glass bowl

indicators.note: something imbibed is drunk in, so the abbreviation is taken inside the other letters
all mixed says every letter so far is stirred together into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: An odd diet of rum, tons of it drunk from an antique glass bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatretum is a Roman cage cup, a glass bowl carved with an openwork outer shell.

clue.text: Fungal mass trod in a mess round track shortly? (6, two words)

indicators.note: a thing in a mess is disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled
round means going around, so the jumble encloses the other piece
shortly means in short form, so the word is cut to its abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
track here is a railway, whose abbreviation RY keeps its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A walker tramps a fungal growth into a muddy railway path.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that destroys timber, spreading as a spongy mass of threads through wood.

clue.text: Herd's wandering round fixed course, cowboy's choice?

indicators.note: wandering means straying from its course, so the letters roam into a new order
round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
a rut is a fixed routine or groove

explanation.surface: Cattle drifting off a set trail, leaving the cowboy to pick which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that druthers is a folksy American word, the sort a cowboy might use.
explanation.definitionFit: Druthers, from would rather, is US colloquial for one's preference, as in if I had my druthers.

clue.text: Ulster's symbol had broken apart in split (7, two words)

indicators.note: a thing broken apart is smashed into fragments, so these letters are reassembled differently
in places the jumbled letters within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
to rend is to tear apart or split

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland's emblem has been torn in two in a division.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Hand of Ulster is the heraldic emblem of the province, a raised open red hand.

clue.text: Mould to fatten manure

blocks.note: first meaning: earth, loose ground
second meaning: to feed livestock on fresh green fodder
third meaning: dung or compost

explanation.surface: Instructions to shape something so as to fatten up dung.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition. Mould is the old word for loose earth, as in leaf mould.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers earth, the farming verb for feeding cattle on green fodder, and excrement or manure.

clue.text: Netted luce, treat I cooked

indicators.note: cooked food has been worked over and transformed, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Having caught a pike in a net, I prepared it as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Luce is an old name for the pike, a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticulate means netted, marked with a network of lines like a mesh.

clue.text: E.g. peach in stew is bubbling, displaying savvy

indicators.note: in places the example inside the jumbled letters
bubbling liquid churns about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: a peach is an example of a fruit tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peach simmering in a bubbling stew, served by a cook who knows their stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: E.g. peach looks like fruit for the stew, but it means a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise describes someone shrewd in urban ways, having practical savvy about how to survive.

clue.text: Barley dish, mass in a fibre turned over

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation within the fibre
turned over in a down clue means flipped, so the whole sequence reads back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
bast is the fibrous inner bark of trees, used for matting and rope
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A cereal dish with loads of fibre, which someone turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes after the B of BAST; A comes in front, and the lot reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsamba (tsampa) is the Tibetan staple of roasted barley flour, usually mixed with butter tea.

clue.text: Key, by the sound of it, for embroidery decoration

indicators.note: by the sound of it means judge by ear, so we want a word pronounced like the synonym

blocks.note: a key (or cay) is a small low island, an islet, whose s is silent

explanation.surface: A tune's key, heard in passing, as a motif to stitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Key here is the island sense, as in the Florida Keys, not a lock or music.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole edged with stitching, a decorative feature of broderie anglaise.

clue.text: Complaint about a Maori woman

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes around the next

blocks.note: a whine is a moaning complaint
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble concerning a New Zealand woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside WHINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wahine is the Maori word for a woman or wife, used widely in New Zealand English.

clue.text: Ruffians delivering last of beating and suchlike

indicators.note: delivering means handing over, so the ruffians give up a letter
last of points to the final letter of the following word as the one surrendered

blocks.note: thugs are violent ruffians
the final letter of beating

explanation.surface: Hooligans dishing out a final thrashing and that kind of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G from THUGS. Delivering is read as handing over, not as inflicting a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this way or so, and suchlike is used loosely for similar manner.

clue.text: Tidy skill shown in backing businessman

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the combined pieces read from right to left

blocks.note: red (or redd) is a dialect verb meaning to tidy up
art is a skill or knack

explanation.surface: Neat craftsmanship on show in the support of a commercial venture.
explanation.walkthrough: RED plus ART, read backwards. Red, to tidy, is Scots and Northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is someone who buys and sells goods for a living, a merchant or dealer.

clue.text: Jock's pet took a walk almost, climbing

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun meaning sulks; pet is a fit of sulking

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
climbing in a down clue means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: strode is past tense of stride, to walk with long steps

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's dog went out for a walk, almost reaching the top of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet is not an animal but a huff; Jock is a crossword name for a Scot, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, the dorts means the sulks, a fit of petulance, which is what a pet is.

clue.text: Some bones swallowed in haunches

indicators.note: in places the swallowed word inside the other

blocks.note: the hams are the backs of the thighs, the haunches
ate is past tense of eat, to swallow food

explanation.surface: Bones gulped down along with haunches of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamates are hooked wrist bones, so named for the hook-like process each carries.

clue.text: Clay-chalk mixture in normal manufacture

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the following run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A clay and chalk blend made in the standard way.
explanation.definitionFit: Malm is a soft chalky loam, and also a brick-making blend of clay and chalk.

clue.text: Wagons feature? Guardsman shows this regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A guard on a train's carriages keeps showing off this detail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wagon (or Wain) is an old name for the Plough, which forms part of the constellation Ursa Major.
explanation.definitionFit: The star pattern known as the Wain or Wagon is a feature of the Great Bear constellation.

clue.text: Chinese weight, requiring muscle to lift round East

indicators.note: to lift in a down clue means raise, so the letters read bottom to top
round means surrounding, so the raised word goes around the abbreviation

blocks.note: lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A heavy oriental weight needs a strong back to raise it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tael is a traditional unit of weight in China and East Asia, also used for silver currency.

clue.text: Designation in wing coating

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: a name is a designation
an el is a wing built at right angles to a main building, so named for its L shape

explanation.surface: A title painted onto the wing of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The wing is not an aircraft's but a building's: an el is an extension built at right angles.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glassy protective layer fused onto metal, or the hard outer layer of teeth.

clue.text: Jail senior naval officer for corruption in Scotland

blocks.note: stir is slang for prison
RA is Rear Admiral

explanation.surface: Lock up a high-ranking naval officer on charges of corruption north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Corruption looks like bribery but means a corrupted form of a word: stirra is a Scots variant of sirrah.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirra is recorded as a Scottish corrupted form of sirrah, the contemptuous term of address.

clue.text: China product, terribly steep, including a lot of wine?

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly damaged, so these letters are knocked into a new order
including means taking in, so the jumble holds the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a tun is a large cask for wine, holding a great deal

explanation.surface: Chinese goods at outrageous prices, plus a lot of wine thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country (and it is the origin), but the product is for making porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Petuntse is a feldspathic china stone, ground and mixed with kaolin to make hard-paste porcelain.

clue.text: Chap in group with uncle once conveying what amounts to an idea

indicators.note: in places the chap inside the group

blocks.note: a set is a group
a chap is a man
eme is an obsolete word for uncle

explanation.surface: A fellow in a gathering with his old uncle, getting an idea across.
explanation.walkthrough: Eme is an obsolete word for uncle, a favourite of Azed.
explanation.definitionFit: A semanteme is a unit of meaning in linguistics, the element carrying a concept or notion.

clue.text: Large Indian tree, a willow, not short

indicators.note: not says to go without the word that follows, so it is taken away

blocks.note: a sallow is a kind of willow
short in height is low

explanation.surface: A big Indian tree, and a willow that is quite tall.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LOW from SALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The sal is a tall Indian timber tree, valued for hard durable wood like teak.
